os-efcore-sqlite.title: SQLite
os-efcore-sqlite.summary: A database in one file next to your app, with no server to install. Safe connection settings, optional encryption of the whole file, and dates that sort correctly.

gives.1: One line gives you a context on a SQLite file with foreign keys, WAL, a wait for busy writers and a sensible sync level already set.
gives.2: Encrypt the whole file with a key that lives only as long as the user's session, and manage encrypted files through a small vault.
gives.3: Dates you can sort and filter, and SQLite errors turned into the same `data.*` results as every other database.

sample.register: A context on a SQLite file
sample.encrypted: An encrypted file with a key from the session
sample.in-memory: A database in memory, for tools and tests

connection.title: Connecting and tuning
connection.summary: Give a path or ask for memory; the connection settings are applied each time a connection opens.

1.title: Settings on every open
1.text: SQLite forgets most settings, so they are applied each time the file opens.

2.title: Busy wait
2.text: `BusyTimeout` is how long a writer waits before the save returns `data.busy`.

4.title: Fixed statements
4.text: Nothing you pass is pasted into SQL.

1.title: What is applied
1.text:
SQLite is a file, so 'connecting' means opening the file with the right settings, and SQLite forgets most settings when a connection closes. `AddOSSqlite` registers your context through the core, so stamps, history, errors and transactions all work.

On every open it applies, in order: the encryption key (if you use one), then foreign keys on (SQLite leaves them off by default), a busy wait so a second writer waits instead of failing at once, WAL for files so readers never wait for the writer, and the sync level.

2.title: Sync level
2.text:
`Normal` is the usual choice with WAL; use `Full` when every commit must survive a power cut, at some cost in speed.

The settings use fixed statements only; nothing you pass is pasted into SQL.

3.title: Path, waiting and retry
3.text:
Set either `Path` or `InMemory`, never both. SQLite has no network, so there is no retry strategy.

`BusyTimeout` is how long a writer waits, and the EF command timeout from `EFCoreOptions` is the outer limit. If the wait runs out, the save returns `data.busy`. `UseOSSqlite` does the same for a builder you make yourself.

tune.title: Wait time and sync level
tune.note: Three seconds of waiting for another writer, and `Full` sync for data that must survive a power cut.

manual.title: Set up a builder yourself
manual.note: For a tool or a test that builds its own context. Call `UseOS` after it so the save pipeline is added.

type.SqliteOptions: Where the database is and how its connections behave.
type.SqliteSynchronous: How hard SQLite works to keep a commit through a power cut.

SqliteOptions.Path: The database file, relative or absolute. Required unless `InMemory` is set. The folder must exist.
SqliteOptions.InMemory: A database in memory that lives as long as the app. Cannot be encrypted.
SqliteOptions.Key: A function that returns the encryption key for each new connection. Leave it null for a plain file.
SqliteOptions.BusyTimeout: How long a writer waits for another writer. 5 seconds by default, at most 5 minutes.
SqliteOptions.WriteAheadLog: Uses WAL for files so readers and the writer do not block each other. On by default.
SqliteOptions.Pooling: Keeps connections open for reuse. On by default.

SqliteSynchronous.Off: No syncing. Fastest; a power cut can corrupt the file. Only for throwaway data.
SqliteSynchronous.Normal: The usual choice with WAL: safe against crashes; a power cut can lose the last commit.
SqliteSynchronous.Full: Every commit is synced. Survives a power cut; a little slower.
SqliteSynchronous.Extra: Like Full with one more sync step, for the most careful setups.

SqliteEx.AddOSSqlite: Registers a context on SQLite. Registers OS.EFCore too when it is not registered yet, so one call is enough; call `AddOSEFCore` as well, before or after, only to change its settings.
SqliteEx.UseOSSqlite: Applies the SQLite setup to a builder.
SqliteEx.NowTicksSql: SQLite's current UTC time in the same ticks format as stored dates, for a column default.

encryption.title: Encrypting the file
encryption.summary: Encrypt every page of the file; without the key it cannot be read, even by copying it.

1.title: Useless copies
1.text: An encrypted file is useless without the key.

3.title: Key as function
3.text: `Key` is read only when a connection opens.

1.title: Why and how
1.text:
A SQLite file can be copied off a laptop or a backup. With encryption, the copy is useless without the key. The package uses SQLite3 Multiple Ciphers with ChaCha20-Poly1305 and a key stretched by PBKDF2 with 256,000 rounds.

These settings are fixed, because they are part of the file format: changing them would make existing files unreadable, and files made by the older framework still open.

2.title: The key
2.text:
A key needs at least 12 characters. Give the key as a function, `Key`, so it is read only when a connection opens and never sits in the connection string or in the long-lived pooled options.

When the user signs out or the key changes, call `ISqliteVault.Close()` so no pooled connection keeps the key.

3.title: ISqliteVault
3.text:
`ISqliteVault` also tells whether a file is missing, plain or encrypted by reading its header, checks a key, encrypts a plain file and changes the key; these return an `OSResult` with a code from `SqliteCodes`.

A wrong key or a damaged file gives `data.offline` on save, never a crash, and neither the key nor the path appears in a result or in our logs.

key-stays-out.title: The key never appears in the connection string
key-stays-out.note: The file is encrypted, and the connection string does not contain the key.

encrypt.title: Encrypt a plain file
encrypt.note: Only a plain file can be encrypted; otherwise the result says `sqlite.notPlain`.

change-key.title: Change the key
change-key.note: The current key is checked first; pooled connections are closed afterwards.

sign-in.title: Check a key at sign-in
sign-in.note: False for a wrong key, a short key or a file that is not encrypted.

sign-out.title: Close everything at sign-out
sign-out.note: After this no pooled connection keeps the key in memory.

type.ISqliteVault: Checks, encrypts and re-keys SQLite files.
type.SqliteFileState: Whether a file is missing, plain or encrypted.
type.SqliteCodes: The result codes of the vault.

ISqliteVault.Probe: Reads the first bytes of the file and tells whether it is missing, plain or encrypted. Needs no key.
ISqliteVault.CanOpenAsync: Whether a key opens an encrypted file.
ISqliteVault.EncryptAsync: Encrypts a plain file with a key, then turns WAL back on.
ISqliteVault.ChangeKeyAsync: Moves an encrypted file to a new key after checking the current one.
ISqliteVault.Close: Closes all pooled SQLite connections in the app.

SqliteFileState.Missing: No file, or an empty one.
SqliteFileState.Encrypted: No readable header, so the file is encrypted.

SqliteCodes.KeyTooShort: The key has fewer than 12 characters.
SqliteCodes.KeyRejected: The current key does not open the file.
SqliteCodes.NotPlain: The file is not a plain database, so it cannot be encrypted again.

notes.title: Dates, errors and logs
notes.summary: Where SQLite behaves differently, what errors come back, and one logging tip.

1.title: Dates as ticks
1.text: Dates are stored as UTC ticks and filter in SQL.

2.title: Error mapping
2.text: SQLite codes map to the usual `data.*` results.

3.title: Debug logs
3.text: EF's Debug logs can show the file path; filter that category.

4.title: Real files
4.text: Every test of this package runs on real files.

1.title: Dates
1.text: SQLite cannot compare `DateTimeOffset` values, so every date is stored as UTC ticks, a number that sorts correctly. `Where` and `OrderBy` on dates run in SQL and values come back as UTC.

2.title: Error mapping
2.text: Errors are mapped from SQLite's own codes, checked on sqlite.org: a taken unique or primary key value gives `data.duplicate` with the column, a missing value `data.required`, a foreign key `data.missingRef` (or `data.inUse` when deleting), a busy or locked database `data.busy`, and a wrong key or damaged file `data.offline`.

3.title: Logs and tests
3.text:
EF's own Debug-level connection logs can show the file path; if you send Debug logs anywhere, filter that category.

Every test of this package runs on real files.

date-storage.title: How a date is stored
date-storage.note: The column holds an integer (UTC ticks), and the value comes back with offset zero.

hide-debug-paths.title: Keep file paths out of Debug logs
hide-debug-paths.note: Raises the minimum level of EF's connection log category.
